title: Fever in a kidney transplant recipient — focused assessment and safe immediate decisions

blocks.text: Fever in a kidney transplant recipient — focused assessment and safe immediate decisions
AMaC MRCP PACES23 • R5-220 • Station 2 acute consultation • Skills A–G plus relevant assessment • 20 minutes • 14 October 2026 • Educational assessment, not official PACES marking

A 44-year-old kidney-transplant recipient taking tacrolimus, mycophenolate and prednisolone develops fever and malaise. Take a focused history, explain your differential and initiate a safe management plan.

sections.heading: 4. The Hook and the Examiner Trap

blocks.text:
Hook: Infection in an immunosuppressed transplant recipient, including bacterial urinary infection and CMV disease; consider rejection if graft dysfunction, but fever alone does not diagnose rejection.
Trap: Hypotension, rigors, organ dysfunction or falling urine output requires immediate admission and senior review. Do not independently stop baseline immunosuppression or prescribe a macrolide without checking tacrolimus interactions.

rows: “First I want to check how unwell you are.”
ABCDE and vital signs as indicated.
“May I ask about these symptoms and exposures?”
Ask when transplanted, immunosuppression and adherence, urinary and respiratory symptoms, graft pain, sick contacts and recent antimicrobials; check sepsis observations and graft tenderness.
“There are several causes, including one requiring prompt treatment.”
Infection in an immunosuppressed transplant recipient, including bacterial urinary infection and CMV disease; consider rejection if graft dysfunction, but fever alone does not diagnose rejection.
“I will arrange urgent tests and care.”

Obtain cultures, FBC, CRP, kidney function, urinalysis/culture, tacrolimus trough and CMV PCR as clinically appropriate; involve transplant team immediately; follow sepsis guidance and assess drug interactions.

Explains serious bacterial infection and opportunistic infection, including CMV
Includes graft pyelonephritis, rejection and drug toxicity depending on evidence
Obtains blood and urine cultures, FBC, renal function and appropriate infection tests promptly
Discusses tacrolimus levels and transplant-team-guided CMV testing
Starts sepsis treatment when indicated, including prompt antimicrobials under local guidance
Contacts transplant team before changing immunosuppression and adjusts medicines for renal function

blocks.text: Patient is worried and asks “Could this be serious?” Only disclose clinical information if elicited. Respond to calm explanations; ask whether hospital assessment is necessary. Do not introduce a diagnosis the candidate has not explored.

THINK: Infection in an immunosuppressed transplant recipient, including bacterial urinary infection and CMV disease; consider rejection if graft dysfunction, but fever alone does not diagnose rejection. SAY: explain uncertainty. DO: Obtain cultures, FBC, CRP, kidney function, urinalysis/culture, tacrolimus trough and CMV PCR as clinically appropriate; involve transplant team immediately; follow sepsis guidance and assess drug interactions. NUMBERS: PACES 20-minute encounter. TRAP: avoid premature reassurance. FINISH: Hypotension, rigors, organ dysfunction or falling urine output requires immediate admission and senior review. Do not independently stop baseline immunosuppression or prescribe a macrolide without checking tacrolimus interactions.
